mechanics.name: Inner Focus
mechanics.currentEffect: You can always see other Survivors' Scratch Marks. Whenever another Survivor loses a Health State due to the Killer, the Killer's Aura is revealed to you for 6/8/10 seconds, depending on perk tier.
activation: Scratch Mark visibility is continuously available during the Trial.
For the Killer Aura reveal, another Survivor must lose a Health State due to the Killer.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (8.3.2): The Killer Aura reveal now triggers only from Health State loss caused by the Killer; 8.3.0 had increased the reveal duration to 6/8/10 seconds and removed its 32 m condition.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: It shows teammates' Scratch Marks and briefly reveals the Killer when the Killer causes a teammate to lose a Health State.
duration: Killer Aura reveal: 6/8/10 seconds per qualifying event.

editorial.summary: Always see teammates' Scratch Marks; whenever the Killer makes another Survivor lose a Health State, see the Killer for up to 10 seconds.
useCases: Track where teammate chases are moving through their Scratch Marks.
Gain a long Killer Aura read every time another Survivor loses a Health State.
Use the hit-triggered Aura to judge whether the Killer is continuing chase or rotating.
counters: Provides no Aura trigger when you are the Survivor losing the Health State.
Team Scratch Marks can add visual clutter.
Stealth and Aura-blocking Killer effects can deny the read.
pros: Ten-second Killer Aura reads are long.
Natural trigger occurs frequently in normal matches.
cons: Does less while you are the primary chase target.
analysis: Inner Focus earns this position because a ten-second Killer Aura reveal after a teammate loses a Health State is a substantial information window. Hits are among the most common events in the game, so the perk receives opportunities without demanding unusual setup.

The permanent teammate Scratch Marks add another layer. They can tell you where a teammate recently ran even after their Aura disappears, helping infer chase paths or avoid colliding with another Survivor's pressure.
Solo Q benefits more than SWF because the perk supplies information a coordinated team can often communicate verbally. Even in SWF, a ten-second Killer Aura is more precise than a callout.
It remains in B because the information is mostly reactive. You gain knowledge after the Killer has already created pressure, and the perk offers no direct way to stop the next hit.
editorial.verdict: A strong reactive information perk. Inner Focus gives long Killer reads off normal match events and is especially useful when Solo Q lacks chase callouts.
